reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraph.

The rule's preferred position is 'no non-solicit on Customer'; the document contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding the Client, so the preferred position is satisfied and no negotiation issue arises.

The cited paragraph (§ d, Use of Credit Data) is the closest restrictive-covenant touchpoint (it references a separate Non-Competition Agreement) and, as the rationale correctly states, restricts use of Credit Data rather than hiring or soliciting personnel — it does not create a personnel restriction.

The failed deterministic checks (no duration found, no general-solicitation carve-out) are consistent with, not contradictory to, the absence of any non-solicit clause; they are not evidence of a missed deviation.

Minor observation only: the cross-referenced Non-Competition Agreement is outside this document and could contain personnel restrictions; the rationale already flags this, so it does not undermine the compliant classification.
